subject: OnsiteIQ's Multimodal data management solution
text:
Hi [NAME],

We recently released EMM-1
<[LINK]>
-
the world's largest open-source multimodal dataset, with 107 million image,
video, text, audio and point cloud embeddings - and thought it might be
relevant given the work you're doing.

Our engineering team has been building out dataset curation and label
validation tooling specifically for visual AI teams at your stage of scale
- we're working with teams like OnsiteIQ and would love to get your take on
what we've shipped.

Would you be open to a quick 15-minute chat to take a look, see if there's
any overlap, and share some honest feedback?

subject: Scaling CV team + pipelines | Working w/ AbbVie, Tractable & Intenseye
text:
Hi [NAME],

Saw you're scaling the CV team, with defect detection, quality inspection,
and safety monitoring all in scope.

Tractable and Intenseye came to us when their annotation ops were
bottlenecked; defect ontologies and label consistency stop scaling once you
move past one use case.

Additionally, without a visual way to search for and find rare defects /
edge-case safety scenarios in the data, retraining decisions end up
reactive.

If this is on your radar, it would be worth a 15-min conversation. The
following times work well for me:

   - *Tuesday 28th April*, 10:00
   - *Wednesday 29th April*, 11:00
   - *Wednesday 29th April, *13:00 (I have put in some tentative time here,
   but happy to reschedule according to availability)

subject: Encord <> [COMPANY] | Working w Flatiron Health, AbbVie, Mayo Clinic
text:
Hi [NAME],

Congrats on the Polaris win. Predicting ADMET better than 38 competitors in
a blinded challenge is a strong proof point!

I work at Encord. We see teams in the ML biotech world hit friction when
scaling their training infrastructure and iterating on proprietary
datasets. As the consortium grows and more drug programs come online,
internal tooling slows, infrastructure management costs increase and it
becomes harder for the model to efficiently include active learning.

We're a unified multimodal MLOps platform that helps ML teams manage,
curate, and evaluate training data at scale. We're trusted by Flatiron
Health, Target RWE, AbbVie amongst others.

A conversation might be beneficial for both of us, worth 20 minutes?

subject: Edge case discovery for fake ID detection | Working w/ Onfido & Veriff
text:
Hi [NAME],

Saw the senior CV hire focused on document analysis and anomaly detection
at 100M IDs/year scale. We work with identity and document verification
teams like Onfido and Veriff, so the timing felt worth a note.

Their ML leads came to us when:

   1. False positive rates plateaued because edge cases (altered IDs, novel
   forgeries) were buried in millions of normal scans
   2. Document ontologies across states and regions broke their existing
   annotation tooling
   3. Near real-time HITL workflows left no room for model regressions in
   production

Worth 15 mins to compare notes? Thursdays 11:00-13:00 and Fridays
09:00-12:00 usually work well for me.

subject: UAV false detections with CVAT| Working w/ Skydio, Zipline, Forterra
text:
Hi [NAME],

New AI leaders at autonomous drone companies usually inherit the same
pipeline issues. Three we see most often with teams running CVAT + ClearML
at [COMPANY]' scale:

   1. QA bottlenecks on multimodal (RGB + thermal) data
   2. Thermal false positives slipping through to production
   3. Training cycles stretching as curation lags behind ingestion

Teams we work with like Zipline, Skydio, and Forterra hit similar walls
before moving off CVAT.

Worth 15 min to compare notes? Wednesdays from 15:00-16:00 and Thursdays
from 12:00-14:00 usually work for me.

subject: Intro from Dieter - Encord x Nanoflex
text:
Hi [NAME],

Dieter suggested I reach out, as he mentioned you have closer oversight of
the ML pipeline at Nanoflex and thought a conversation with us would be
worth your time.

Quick context: Encord is the data development platform for computer vision
teams in high-stakes domains. We're used heavily across medical imaging and
surgical robotics for annotation, curation, and model-in-the-loop
workflows, particularly where the imagery isn't standard (fluoroscopy,
angiography, intra-procedural video) and label error has real consequences.

Nanoflex's setup looks like exactly that kind of problem:
catheter/guidewire tracking, vessel-level navigation, magnetic actuation
feedback, all from imagery that doesn't behave like a COCO benchmark. Teams
we work with in adjacent spaces tend to hit the same walls early:
annotation tooling that doesn't handle the modality, data ops that buckle
once volume scales, and review loops with no clean way for engineers or
clinicians to flag bad labels.

Worth a 30-min intro to compare notes? I'd share what we've seen work for
teams in similar spots and learn where you are in yours. I have time next
week, do any of these slots work (CET):

   1. Tuesday 5th May: 1430-1500pm
   2. Wednesday 6th May: 1200 - 1230pm // 1500 - 1530pm

subject: How are you thinking about real-world eval data for VFA?
text:

getting the right attention.

sensor modalities.

call next Wed or Thu?

subject: Encord referral by Sai Kishor
text:
Hi [NAME],

I spoke to Sai from your robotics team last week, and wanted to follow up
as he suggested you'd be the best person to speak to about Encord.

After looking at TIAGo Pro and KANGAROO more closely, the overlap I felt
Encord had with PAL is sharper than I realised. TIAGo Pro is positioned
around teleoperation and data generation for AI training, and KANGAROO is
explicitly your embodied-AI / VLA platform: both are exactly the workloads
Encord is built for.

Just wanted to include some more context on Encord and the work we do with
other humanoid and robotics companies to optimise their model evaluations
and data pipelines. A few specific PAL-relevant angles:

For VLA training on KANGAROO: structured observation-action data across
embodiments, contact-state and motion-primitive labeling, and benchmarking
across model versions so you can see where the policy is actually failing.

For TIAGo Pro teleop pipelines: turning raw demonstration video into
timestamped, model-ingestible action labels (grasp type, contact
transitions, sub-task boundaries) without burning research time on data ops.

For multi-embodiment research programs like COGNITIUM and your other EU
collaboratives: versioned datasets that travel across partners, with clear
ground-truth tracking per model iteration.

Would love to have a more structured conversation next week with yourself
and the team. How do some of the following times work (CET):

   - Tuesday 5th May 1500 - 1530pm
   - Thursday 7th May 1000-1030am // 1400-1430pm
